newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish KGHM unions uphold strike alert, want talks.
newsitem.headline: Polish KGHM unions uphold strike alert, want talks.

text.p: Seven trade unions at Poland's KGHM copper firm decided on Thursday to remain on strike alert to pursue their other demands after KGHM's board agreed to average wage rises on Wednesday, a union official said.

Jozef Czyczerski, head of the Solidarity union, told Reuters the unions still demanded a 10 percent increase of the basic salary in the concern and social guarantees, including a 10-year employment guarantee.

"The unions sent a letter to KGHM's president that the Wednesday average wage rise agreement does not solve all the issues raised by the unions in the collective dispute with the board and the strike alert remains in force," Czyczerski said.
"We wrote that we expect the board to start constructive talks on the issues by April 4," he said.

On Wednesday the board and unions agreed that the average worker's wage of 1,726.59 zlotys would rise by a total of 17 percent in 1997, instead of 15 percent, in two installments -- on April 1 and July 1.
The firm, slated to be floated on the Warsaw and London bourses later this year, has 23,400 workers.

The board of KGHM, one of the world's major copper and silver producers, is not willing to discuss union demands under laws of so-called collective disputes because, it says, there are no legal grounds for the start of a collective dispute.
Polish laws of collective dispute give trade unions a much broader array of instruments in enforcing their demands, including a strike, than a regular negotiation protocol.
The board is willing to talk with the unions only under a regular negotiation protocol, a source close to the talks told Reuters.
